executive_summary: This collection window (July 6 - July 12, 2027) is the fifty-fifth archived window and covers the actual staging of Paris Haute Couture Week FW27, which this index flagged as pre-show anticipation coverage last window. All three creative-director-level debuts previewed on 2027-07-05 -- Pierpaolo Piccioli's first Balenciaga couture collection, Duran Lantink's first Jean Paul Gaultier couture collection, and Olivier Theyskens's new label Boloria -- have now shown and generated real post-show reception coverage, upgrading last window's anticipation signal into a confirmed reception signal. Reception across all three is genuinely mixed rather than uniformly positive: Piccioli's Balenciaga is described as a confident, reverent recalibration that has nonetheless divided audiences loyal to the prior era; Lantink's Gaultier is described in openly polarizing terms, from 'worthy heir' to accusations of a 'cheap imitation'; Theyskens's Boloria drew comparatively narrower but still split notices, praised for craftsmanship while some found it emotionally distant. Met Gala 2027 remains untracked going forward per last window's call -- a targeted check this window surfaced no new theme, co-chair, or red-carpet coverage, consistent with that status rather than reopening it. Wales Bonner/Hermes and CFDA Fashion Fund/Awards were not re-litigated this window per SKILL.md workflow note 10.

top_signals.name: Paris Haute Couture Week FW27 debuts: confirmed post-show reception (Piccioli/Balenciaga, Lantink/Jean Paul Gaultier, Theyskens/Boloria)
top_signals.evidence: All three debuts previewed in the 2027-07-05 report have now shown during Paris Haute Couture Week (July 6-9, 2027) and generated substantive post-show critical coverage. Piccioli's Balenciaga debut is covered as reverent toward Cristobal Balenciaga's archive (neo gazar volumes, cocoon and balloon silhouettes) while opening a distinct new chapter from the prior era, with coverage explicitly noting a divided audience response. Lantink's Jean Paul Gaultier debut is covered as deliberately provocative, drawing reactions from 'worthy heir' framing to explicit criticism calling it a 'cheap imitation' of the house's subversive-but-chic codes. Theyskens's Boloria debut is covered as a tailoring-forward, melancholic collection ('The Row meets Rimbaud') with mixed reviews -- praised for dressmaking craft, criticized by some as emotionally distant.
top_signals.index_note: Classified designer_originated, continuing the 2027-07-05 signal's classification rather than starting a new one: this is the same three debuts moving from pre-show anticipation to confirmed post-show reception, not a new event. Confidence raised from 'medium' to 'high' relative to last window because the underlying claim has shifted from 'these shows will happen and are anticipated' (forward-looking, harder to verify) to 'these shows happened and here is documented critical reaction' (backward-looking, directly verifiable against published reviews). Genuinely mixed/divided reception across all three is reported as such rather than smoothed into a single verdict -- flattening 'divisive' coverage into 'well-received' or 'poorly-received' would misrepresent the actual discourse.
top_signals.human_editor_note: The editorial judgment call here is what NOT to do: it would be easy to round three genuinely split critical receptions into a tidy 'couture week was a triumph' or 'couture week disappointed' narrative for a cleaner report. The actual coverage doesn't support either -- each of the three debuts reads as contested on its own terms (Piccioli: reverent vs. a departure from Demna's era; Lantink: inventive heir vs. cheap imitation; Theyskens: refined craft vs. soulless), and treating three different arguments as one aggregate trend would be the exact kind of flattening this index exists to avoid. Also worth flagging: wallpaper.com, nssmag.com, and theimpression.com are established fashion trade press by any reasonable read but remain outside DOMAIN_SECTOR_MAP, so a chunk of this signal's real corroboration still classifies as 'unclear' sector -- the same taxonomy-coverage gap noted last window, not yet closed.
